title: Review shared domain helper families for embeddings, indexing, search, risk, language, and type/token processing
scope: Primary ownership for src/shared domain helper families assigned to #414 in the shared-module ledger, including embeddings-cache, indexing, filter, fs, hash, perf, text, validation, safe-regex, and root-level domain-specific utilities.

summary.overallAssessment: Most of this surface is genuinely shared and domain-specific rather than a random grab-bag. The strongest parts are the small normalization helpers, backend/config facades, embeddings-cache family, safe-regex backend structure, and low-level perf/text/validation helpers. The main weaknesses are a handful of oversized mixed-responsibility modules and two cross-layer ownership seams: src/shared/dict-utils.js is only a re-export of tools/shared/dict-utils.js, and token-id.js mixes 64-bit token hashing with a specialized typed posting map implementation.

runtimeRisks.reason: This is the largest file in the owned surface and mixes ONNX session setup, provider selection, model loading, input normalization, batch execution, and output handling.
This is a policy-heavy indexing runtime module where timeout classification, budget-extension rules, and progress interpretation are coupled together.
Adapter selection, provider normalization, request shaping, and fallback behavior are mixed in one file that directly affects embedding runtime behavior.
Artifact naming, binary serialization, JSONL sharding, binary hydration, and dense-vector materialization all live together.
Active generation selection, manifest freshness, and build-root pointer semantics are correctness-critical and currently mixed in one file.
Stemming, identifier splitting, punctuation extraction, dictionary segmentation, and n-gram helpers are mixed into one very broad tokenization surface.

maintainabilityOnlyNotes.reason: This is only a cross-layer re-export of tools/shared/dict-utils.js and should not remain as a root src/shared alias.
The typed open-addressed posting map does not belong in the same module as generic token-id hashing helpers.
Useful shared logic, but it is broad enough that normalization and rendering/summary concerns should likely separate over time.

highestPriorityFollowUps.reason: Remove the src/shared-to-tools/shared re-export seam by either moving the real implementation into src/shared or relocating callers back to the tool-side module.
Move the specialized typed posting map into a postings-focused module and leave token-id.js as the hash/id helper surface.
Separate model/session lifecycle, runtime/provider resolution, request shaping, and output normalization.
Separate policy classification, budget math, and progress-state interpretation into narrower indexing runtime helpers.
Separate adapter registry, request normalization, and fallback/runtime policy so embedding provider behavior is easier to reason about.
Separate artifact naming/metadata, binary write/load operations, and row materialization concerns under a denser vector-io family.
Separate active-generation pointer resolution from freshness and manifest compatibility helpers.
Separate identifier tokenization, dictionary segmentation, punctuation extraction, and n-gram helpers into clearer submodules.
